title: Split ingest processor and introduce reactive load-shedder for tenant degradation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Our single-threaded ingest processor mixes fanout/lease coordination, payload preparation, and retry orchestration in the same execution path. This creates three practical issues: (1) noisy head-of-line blocking when long-running handler work stalls leases; (2) coupling between retry semantics and leasing that complicates tenant-level backpressure behavior; and (3) difficulty applying targeted degradation policies (e.g., per-tenant soft-drop) because the processor has no clear demarcation between admission and execution.

Goal: Refactor the ingest pipeline into two orthogonal components: (A) a lightweight ingress coordinator responsible for admission, lease/slot assignment, and fast-path handoffs; and (B) a separate execution worker pool responsible for running handlers, retries, and durable ack semantics. Introduce a reactive load-shedder that operates at the admission layer to apply tiered degradation (reject, delay, or sample) per tenant when cluster-wide signals indicate sustained pressure.

Design decisions and trade-offs: 
- Use Redis mostly for durable lease bookkeeping and fast token buckets; keep Kafka consumers as durable event sources but reduce synchronous handoffs to Redis by using an ephemeral local admission cache. This reduces cross-network hop latency at admission.
- Prefer cooperative cancellation and soft timeouts in execution workers rather than hard-killing leases; this simplifies in-flight cleanup but requires careful idempotency guarantees on handlers.
- The load-shedder will rely on aggregated metrics (ingest queue length, avg handler latency, failure rate) drawn from the observability pipeline. We accept eventual consistency in the shedding decision to avoid centralized locks.
- We will add a tenant-scoped penalty score that increases with retries and failure rate; higher penalty increases probability of sampling/dropping. This is intentionally probabilistic to avoid sharp edges and enable gradual rollout.

Migration plan: 
1) Implement ingress coordinator with feature flag and shadow mode to mirror current routing.
2) Implement execution worker pool behind a new queue consumer abstraction and route a small percentage of traffic via canary.
3) Enable load-shedder in observe-only mode to generate recommended actions and surface them in the console.
4) Soft-enable shedding for low-tier tenants (5%) and iterate based on SLO and error budgets.
5) Full cutover once metrics show reduced tail latency and controlled error ramp.

Acceptance criteria (non-exhaustive): 
- Mean end-to-end enqueue-to-ack latency under synthetic load improves by >= 15% compared to baseline.
- Tail (p99) handler execution latency decreases on average by >= 20% for mixed workloads.
- During a sustained worker-saturation test, the reactive shedder reduces ingress accepted requests for targeted tenant buckets to keep overall error budget within thresholds.
- No increase in data-loss incidents (durable ack semantics preserved).

Notes: This ticket intentionally avoids large Redis client upgrades that would be covered in a separate dependency-upgrade ticket; aim is isolation of control-plane behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Ingress coordinator behind flag that mirrors current routing in shadow mode
Execution worker pool with separate lease-to-executor handoff and explicit ack/clean semantics
Reactive load-shedder emits console metrics and can be toggled to recommended/active modes
Performance tests show >=15% mean latency and >=20% p99 execution latency improvement in target scenarios
No increase in durable ack related incidents during canary (observed for two full canary windows)
comments: 2026-02-19 - Spike: 2d prototype showed admission latency cut by ~18% when moving lease checks out of handler path (Connor).
2026-02-24 - Architecture review: PM and observability raised concerns about too-frequent shedding flips; agreed to add hysteresis and tenant-penalty decay (Lena Fischer).

2026-03-02 - Implementation: added new ingress coordinator service and local admission cache. Initial unit tests green; integration tests failing on flaky Redis timeouts under extreme load (investigating) (Connor).

2026-03-05 - Perf run: synthetic mixed workload shows decrease in head-of-line blocking, but p99 spikes remain for long-running handlers. Decided to introduce per-executor cooperative-cancellation and increase worker pool elasticity. (Asha)

2026-03-08 - Code review: PR #4478 created (https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4478). Feedback: split some helper functions into shared module and add stronger idempotency assertions in handler contract (requested by reviewer: Miguel Santos).

2026-03-12 - Canary start: 3% traffic routed through new pipeline with load-shedder in observe-only mode. Dashboard link: https://console.redwood.com/dashboards/queue-refactor/canary-558812. Initial metrics stable.
2026-03-12 - Next: resolve Redis flakiness by adding connection pool backoff and retry jitter; plan a follow-up perf run focused on p99 handler tail.
